intake.notes:
Buyer is the VP of Operations and Supply Chain at Liquid Death. They sell canned water, sparkling water, flavored sparkling water, and iced tea through retail, distributor, ecommerce, and marketplace channels.

The team needs a demo that proves beverage availability and replenishment confidence across fast-moving retail demand, distributor commitments, and production planning. They care about keeping finished canned beverage availability, case-pack inventory, retail commitments, and co-manufacturing or production timing aligned without creating manual handoffs between sales, finance, and operations.

Current pain: demand moves quickly by channel, but supply planning, inventory availability, and customer commitments can become disconnected. The team needs one operating view of what is available, what is committed, what needs replenishment, and what production or co-manufacturing detail is ready to support the promise.

The demo should show a customer order for a finished canned beverage, the finished beverage item, supporting ingredient/component or packaging item if returned, replenishment or availability flow, and WIP/work order detail only if available. If WIP detail is not returned, keep the story honest and say WIP detail was not returned.

ROI angle: reduce manual reconciliation between sales demand, distributor commitments, inventory, and production planning; improve confidence in available-to-promise; reduce avoidable stockouts or late replenishment; protect service levels during high-velocity retail demand spikes.

Competitive angle: show that FORGE can create a beverage proof path grounded in website evidence and selected toggles, not generic hardgoods or apparel naming. The story should use beverage, canned drink, finished item, replenishment, ingredient/component, packaging, availability, and production-planning language only when supported by the website and selected toggles.

customer.name: Liquid Death
customer.notes:
Buyer is the VP of Operations and Supply Chain at Liquid Death. They sell canned water, sparkling water, flavored sparkling water, and iced tea through retail, distributor, ecommerce, and marketplace channels.

The team needs a demo that proves beverage availability and replenishment confidence across fast-moving retail demand, distributor commitments, and production planning. They care about keeping finished canned beverage availability, case-pack inventory, retail commitments, and co-manufacturing or production timing aligned without creating manual handoffs between sales, finance, and operations.

Current pain: demand moves quickly by channel, but supply planning, inventory availability, and customer commitments can become disconnected. The team needs one operating view of what is available, what is committed, what needs replenishment, and what production or co-manufacturing detail is ready to support the promise.

The demo should show a customer order for a finished canned beverage, the finished beverage item, supporting ingredient/component or packaging item if returned, replenishment or availability flow, and WIP/work order detail only if available. If WIP detail is not returned, keep the story honest and say WIP detail was not returned.

ROI angle: reduce manual reconciliation between sales demand, distributor commitments, inventory, and production planning; improve confidence in available-to-promise; reduce avoidable stockouts or late replenishment; protect service levels during high-velocity retail demand spikes.

Competitive angle: show that FORGE can create a beverage proof path grounded in website evidence and selected toggles, not generic hardgoods or apparel naming. The story should use beverage, canned drink, finished item, replenishment, ingredient/component, packaging, availability, and production-planning language only when supported by the website and selected toggles.
